newsitem.title: USA: Boeing shareholders approve McDonnell Douglas deal.
newsitem.headline: Boeing shareholders approve McDonnell Douglas deal.

text.p: Boeing Co. shareholders on Friday approved the $15 billion merger between the aerospace giant and McDonnell Douglas Corp..
Over 99 percent of voting shareholders approved the deal, the company said at a special meeting of shareholders.
McDonnell Douglas shareholders were scheduled to vote on the merger at a separate meeting Friday.

Boeing won European Union approval of its plan to acquire McDonnell Douglas earlier this week after making some concessions in an 11th-hour deal. It agreed not to sign any exclusive sales contracts with airlines for 10 years and to scrap sole-supplier contracts with AMR Corp.'s American Airlines, Continental Airlines Inc. and Delta Air Lines Inc..
Boeing has said it believes the concessions would have little if any impact on the increased profits it expects after it closes the merger.
Boeing has said shareholder approval will clear the way for the deal to close on Aug. 1.
